hook: Arthur Samuel trained as an electrical engineer at MIT before spending nearly two decades at Bell Telephone Laboratories working on vacuum tubes and related electronics. After a period teaching at the University of Illinois, he joined IBM in 1949, where he worked on the design of the IBM 701 and 704 computers. In his own time at IBM he wrote a program that played checkers, and rather than encoding a fixed strategy he had it improve through repeated self-play, adjusting its evaluation of board positions based on outcomes and building a memory of positions it had already assessed. He described the work in a 1959 paper in the IBM Journal of Research and Development, using the phrase machine learning to describe a computer's ability to improve at a task without being explicitly reprogrammed for it. Samuel demonstrated an early version of the program on television in 1956, and it stood for years as a widely cited proof that a machine could improve through experience. He moved to Stanford University in 1966, where he continued refining the checkers program and working on computing research until his death in 1990.

Worked on the design of the IBM 701 and 704 computers after joining IBM in 1949
Demonstrated an early version of his checkers program on television in 1956
Received the IEEE Computer Pioneer Award in 1987 for adaptive non-numeric processing

achievements.title: Self-learning checkers program
achievements.impact: Demonstrated that a computer program could improve its performance at a game through self-play and experience rather than through hand-coded strategy alone.

achievements.title: Coined the term machine learning
achievements.impact: His 1959 paper gave the field one of its foundational names and framed learning as a capability a computer could acquire through practice.

achievements.title: Rote learning and generalization techniques
achievements.impact: Introduced methods for storing and reusing evaluations of previously seen board positions, an early form of memoization combined with function approximation.

achievements.title: IEEE Computer Pioneer Award, 1987
achievements.impact: Recognized for adaptive non-numeric processing, honoring his contributions to machine learning research.
